questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Christmas food and dishes around the world
Why Christmas is becoming more expensive
How to buy the perfect Christmas present
Christmas memories, traditions and nostalgia
questions.why: Neil says they'll talk about nostalgia as well as Christmas memories and traditions.

questions.q: What happy Christmas memory does Beth share?
options: Putting on a Christmas show with her cousins
Living in Canada where it always snowed
Cooking Christmas dinner with her dad
Waiting on the stairs for Santa Claus
questions.why: Beth says she and her cousins used to put on a Christmas performance for the family.

questions.q: Why were Neil's childhood Christmases so special?
options: He got lots of presents
He spent them with his cousins
He lived in Canada, where it always snowed
His family went abroad every year
questions.why: Neil lived in Canada as a kid and it was always snowing, so it felt perfect.

options: A feeling of being bored with the present
Feeling happy and sad at once about the past
A fear of the future and what it might bring
Only feeling sad about the past, never happy
questions.why: He says thinking about the past can make us feel happy and sad at the same time.

questions.q: What tradition did Daryl O'Connor's father have on Christmas morning?
options: The children opened all their presents in bed
The family went for a long walk in the snow
The children put out snacks for Santa and his deer
They queued on the stairs while he checked for Santa
questions.why: He says they queued on the stairs while his father checked the front room in case Santa was still there.

questions.q: What does Daryl's story show about nostalgia?
options: It can make people repeat childhood traditions
It makes people forget their old traditions
It only really affects older people
It makes Christmas less fun for children
questions.why: Asked if nostalgia influences his plans, he says 'indeed it does' and he repeats the same tradition.

questions.q: What does Professor Catherine Loveday say about nostalgic memories?
options: They are usually completely accurate and clear
They're often more positive than reality was
They are mostly sad and painful for people
They slowly disappear as we get older
questions.why: She says they're often going to be rose-tinted and made more positive.

questions.q: Why does Catherine think it doesn't matter if our memories aren't accurate?
options: Because nobody else can check them anyway
Because we forget most of them anyway
Memory isn't for accuracy; it suits who we are now
Because only facts and dates are important
questions.why: She says the function of memory is not accuracy, and it's better to adjust memories to suit who we are.
